subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Brushless DC: Electronic Commutation
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Brushless DC: Electronic Commutation.

hook.text: Replace brushes with transistors and a sensor. The motor lasts ten times longer.

buildup.text: Hall sensors detect rotor position. A controller energizes the correct stator coil.

discovery.text: The permanent magnets are on the rotor. The switching happens in the stator — electronically.

twist.text: No brushes means no sparks, no dust, and quieter operation.

climax.text: Computer fans, electric bikes, and industrial robots all run on brushless DC motors.

punchline.text: Transistors replace brushes — electronics made motors silent and durable.

quiz.question: How does a brushless DC motor know when to switch coils?
options: It uses a timer based on the expected rotation speed
Hall effect sensors detect the rotor position and signal the controller
The back-EMF automatically switches the stator current
